revisionHistory.note: Added visually reviewed single-subject political portraits and exotic animal photos. Rejected the three-panel pangolin comparison and two-bird flamingo photo.

revisionHistory.summary: Showed the French title on answer reveal for 132 image-backed art/site entries.

revisionHistory.note: Added reviewed single-subject portraits for ten global political figures and seventeen exotic animals. Campaign-text and group-animal candidates were excluded.
Replaced the multi-character Peter Pan poster and multi-character Forky image with single-character Disney artwork. Both replacements are marked for user review in the image gallery.
Replaced the mother-and-calf sperm whale photo with a single sperm whale photograph from NOAA Fisheries, as requested in the image review.
Replaced the Loki image with an official Marvel character portrait showing the horned helmet and green costume called out in the image review.
Moved the aurora borealis picture question out of Famous Landscapes and into a natural phenomena category, following the gallery review.

Replaced five gallery images flagged in the 2026-10-27 user review: beaver, monarch butterfly, whale shark, Tokyo Skytree, and the Pantheon in Rome. New images retain source and license credits and remain pending user approval in the gallery.
Replaced the horse and pig pictures flagged in the 2026-10-27 image gallery review with full-body animal photos; source credits were recorded and the new versions remain pending user approval.
Updated the remaining written-answer beaver presentation to use the reviewed single-beaver photo already selected for the image Qui suis-je presentation.
Unified animal image questions under one combined image package/category and unified political figure images under one combined image package/category.
Expanded the unified animal image category with individual donkey, goat, domestic cat, mallard duck, and lamb photos to balance rare species with familiar farm and domestic animals.
Replaced the distant incomplete Pantheon view with a full exterior photograph showing the portico and rotunda, addressing the latest gallery review.

Added four single-subject portraits to the unified political-figures image category: Margaret Thatcher, Jacinda Ardern, Mikhail Gorbachev, and John F. Kennedy. Added reusable country and political-role facts with source links.

Applied the newest gallery feedback: replaced the generic Alps image with a distinct Matterhorn question, replaced the female mallard photo with a male drake, and substituted the lower-prominence Jacinda Ardern entry with Indira Gandhi. New images are marked Review.
Replaced the Cleopatra and Julius Caesar photos with clear single-subject museum bust portraits after the latest review requested stronger portraits. Both new images remain pending approval.

Batch-updated Cleopatra, Julius Caesar, and Walden Pond images after repeated replacement feedback. Used single-figure 19th-century paintings for the historical figures and a distinctive photograph of Thoreau’s house at Walden Pond. New images remain pending approval.

Applied latest image-gallery review: used the Caesar portrait specified in the user note; retired Walden Pond and Matterhorn visual QSJ entries per the explicit feedback. Existing written-answer questions remain untouched.
Replaced the difficult aerial sperm-whale photograph with a single full-body NOAA profile illustration that shows the species’ characteristic large head; new image remains pending user review.

Added source-verified, review-pending portraits for requested BD characters, including separate image questions for individual members of selected duos. Pair artwork remains attached only to pair-named questions.
Replaced Conan’s generic portrait with John Buscema’s distinctive comic-art portrait and replaced Natacha’s cropped image with a full-figure text-free crop.

Replaced the five images flagged in review 19: upgraded Laureline and Mélusine portraits, distinct Sylvain and Sylvette portraits, and a Papyrus comic-art image. New gallery images are marked for user approval.

Registered the active René Lévesque image presentation in its question legacyIds. Runtime requires all active presentation IDs to resolve through this alias list; historical aliases remain preserved even when their original presentations are retired.
